newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: VA Stahl sees '96 earnings below '95.
newsitem.headline: VA Stahl sees '96 earnings below '95.

text.p: Austrian steel maker VA Stahl said on Thursday it expected 1996 full year results to be lower than last year's.
"It will be better than 1994 but worse than 1995," chief executive Peter Strahammer reiterated a prediction first made last month. He declined to give further details.
The group reported pre-tax profits of 3.2 billion schillings on sales of 33.8 billion last year, compared to 1.32 billion and 29.88 billion respectively in 1994.

Strahammer, speaking at an investment fair, predicted earnings would slacken in the second half, mainly due to the temporary closure for refurbishment of a plant at the company's headquarters in Linz, upper Austria.

But he said he did not expect a significant decline in production next year. More than half of VA Stahl's business was done through long-term contracts, which meant it was less dependent on the cyclical nature of the steel industry, he added.

Strahammer said the firm could count on losses of "a few hundred million schillings" carried forward to the financial year 1997/98 (to March 31) as a result of the government's scrapping of tax credits on company losses in 1996 and 1997.
Starting next year, the company will reorganise its financial year to begin in March. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
